column2: CAP-21 · Four-states audit across every screen
column3:
Definition of done item 8. A PR with only the happy path is not finished, and by Sprint 5
some of them will have shipped that way anyway. This ticket is where that is found and fixed,
not logged.

Acceptance criteria
* Every screen demonstrates loaded, loading, empty and error. Loading is a skeleton, never a
  spinner.
* The error state surfaces the envelope's message and switches on code where it matters,
  particularly the submit gate, which reports which entries failed.
* A checklist in the PR with a screenshot per state per screen.
* Anything missing is fixed here. Nothing is deferred out of this ticket.

Depends on every screen ticket.

column2: CAP-22 · End-to-end journey test with Playwright
column3:
Definition of done items 2, 3 and 4 proved in one run, through the browser, which is where
the wiring bugs the feature suite cannot see actually live.

Acceptance criteria
* Student creates a reflection, writes every entry, self-scores, is refused an incomplete
  submit with the offending entries named, then submits.
* Assessor sees it in the queue, is forced to comment when scoring below the student, counter-
  scores every entry, and the reflection flips to assessed on its own.
* The radar renders both polygons from real rows afterwards.
* Runs against a seeded test database in CI. Never against the shared instance: the suite
  runs migrate:fresh and five people share that box.

Depends on CAP-11, CAP-13.

Acceptance criteria
* Every interactive element reachable by keyboard with a visible focus ring. Correct roles and
  labels on the stepper and the sheets, which are the two places this usually breaks.
* Contrast AA in both themes, re-checked rather than assumed from CAP-1.
* Usable at 360px and at desktop width.
* The radar has a non-visual equivalent, a table of the same numbers, because colour alone
  cannot carry self versus assessor.

Depends on CAP-21.

column2: CAP-24 · Security review of the frontend and the API seam
column3:
The commitment in the scope document is a security review on every PR touching scoring,
submit or framework mutation. It has been honoured once, on the backend PR. The frontend PRs
that touch all three have not had one.

Acceptance criteria
* Token storage and exposure reviewed, including what ends up in devtools and in logs.
* Narrative, comment and evidence-filename text rendered without injection.
* No client-side role trust anywhere. A hidden nav item and a disabled button are conveniences;
  the 403 and the 409 are the rules.
* Findings raised as tickets rather than fixed silently, and the sign-off recorded.

Depends on CAP-13, CAP-16.

column2: CAP-25 · Contract drift guard in CI
column3:
docs/openapi.yaml and web/src/api/schema.ts drift silently. That is exactly the failure mode
docs/Frontend-and-Backend.md warns about, and right now nothing catches it.

Acceptance criteria
* A CI job regenerates the types from the contract and fails if the committed file differs.
* The existing route-versus-contract comparison runs in the same job.
* Documented in docs/Frontend-and-Backend.md so the next person knows why the job exists.

Depends on CAP-2.

Something to point the client at that is not somebody's laptop.

Acceptance criteria
* The built frontend and the API served over TLS from the VPS.
* The three seeded tokens work against it.
* MYSQL_ATTR_SSL_CA and the mandatory-TLS connection hold in the deployed environment. The
  database refuses unencrypted connections and the failure looks like a wrong password, so
  test this rather than assuming it.
* A documented rollback.
* Nothing secret in the repository, and nothing secret in the deploy config either.

Depends on CAP-21.

column2: CAP-27 · Refresh the ERD and the state tables
column3:
docs/erd.png is three schema changes behind. ADRs #33, #34 and #35 are not on it, including
ak_fw_assignments narrowing from (gig_id, framework_id) to (gig_id). It is the diagram the
client and the marker both look at first.

Acceptance criteria
* Regenerated ERD, with the legend still listing the constraints crow's foot notation cannot
  show, including that a score's level must belong to the entry's competency, which the
  service layer enforces because the database cannot.
* README "Where this is up to" table and the docs/Stack-and-Build-Scope.md checkboxes updated
  to what is actually true, including the [~] items this plan closes.

No dependencies.

Acceptance criteria
* A fixed two-hour session with all five people driving the product as all three roles against
  seeded data. Scheduled, not "when we get a chance".
* Everything found is logged with reproduction steps.
* Triaged into fix-now, fix-if-time, and known-and-accepted.
* The known-and-accepted list is written down. An accepted defect nobody recorded is just a
  defect.

Depends on CAP-26.

column2: CAP-29 · Fresh-clone verification on macOS, Windows and Linux
column3:
Definition of done item 1. Worth its own ticket because run.ps1 has never actually been
executed anywhere, and the Windows path is therefore unproven rather than working.

Acceptance criteria
* Clone, run scripts/setup.sh (and setup.ps1 on Windows), then ./run dev, on all three
  platforms, performed by someone who did not write the script.
* ./run check passes on each.
* Whatever breaks is fixed inside this ticket rather than documented as a workaround.

Depends on CAP-27.

The last ticket on the board. Intellectual property in the delivered solution is assigned to
Alumable, so handover is a real deliverable and not a formality.

Acceptance criteria
* dev merged to main and tagged.
* A runbook: how to start it, where the database lives, how to reseed, how to issue a token.
* Credentials transferred out of band. Never into the repository, and not into a chat log that
  outlives the project either.
* The client demo path written down as a script someone who has never seen the product could
  follow.

Depends on CAP-28, CAP-29.
